about: The allowed exceptions of the import-rules ratchet (packages/core/test/import-rules.test.ts, rules in scripts/audit/lib.mjs). Each group has one rule, a one-line reason and its entries ("<file> → <import>"). A new entry and a stale one both fail the test: after a change, run node scripts/audit/rules.mjs . --write-baseline, write the reason of any new group, and review the diff.

groups.reason: CLI commands drive the adapters themselves (raw export, plan, components, sandboxes, doctor, sign-in checks) until they run on the engine operations.
The Studio's player bundles the compositions with the components and the editor's render entry.
The Studio server reads the component library, themes and edit plans through the adapters until the engine exposes them.
CLI commands read and write files or start processes themselves (init, plan, validate, ui, doctor) until they go through the engine.
The Studio server watches folders, serves files and supervises its worker itself.

P1: the engine still builds these adapters itself; each port (U6) removes entries. 12 file → specifier pairs on 2026-11-12 (L7.11: hooks and review/thumbs went through their ports; L7.12: the runner package through the capture runner's): sandbox 11, components 1.

Elapsed time and deadlines (a scheduler, not a stamp): the worker's idle and build-check timers, waits, grace periods (a cancel's before the kill, an orphan's before recovery), a history line's `ms` (a recording's too), the journal's warn rate limit, the in-memory renderer's render time. Never written as a time; `performance.now()` would do (BACKLOG).
Memo lifetimes kept in memory only (the board's and the scenario view's caches, the Studio's one-time bootstrap codes): compared with the time they were made, never written.
File times: a filming marker's heartbeat and the library cache's recency are compared with the mtimes other processes leave, so they follow the machine's own time.
Outside the engine's contexts: the app set-up (`retake app`, the desktop app) has no composition root of the engine; its backup name takes an injectable `now` already.

Reads of a project folder through the media storage (R-ARC-03), not authored writes: a run's status, a scenario's text (14 callers), a thread view's scenario text, the search index's small files. They move when project reads get a port.

The renderer port still borrows the editor's and the components' types (the registry, bundle components, preview specs, render progress: L7.1 and L7.2, left), until they have a home in core or a domain entry.

The MCP server's tools not yet moved into the engine's operations (U7: 21 of 45 on 2026-11-12, after L7.13 moved the eleven the Studio shares, L7.14 four read-only queries and L7.17 the nine theme and component tools; job_status waits for the record, site and inspect outputs it answers with): they move family by family (L7.15–L7.19) and the group goes.

The Studio's own ops (44 on 2026-11-12, after L7.14 moved its ten read-only queries and L7.17 its eleven theme and library ops): those of a use case the engine serves move into its operations (L7.15–L7.18); the ones that hold the server's own state (its index, player, leases, set-up and update state, unsaved tabs, the desktop pipe: 18 in 6 files) stay here.
Paths spelt as text on purpose: the trust lists (agent-writable paths, a person's files), a new project's .gitignore lines, help texts and the Studio's browser code (no node:path there).

Other names with a grammar of the same shape, each written at its definition and out of the id module: a scenario name (SLUG_RE), a project slug (PROJECT_SLUG_RE), an environment name, a run-folder segment, a review file id.
Hand-written mirrors of the scenario-name and project-slug grammars in the Studio front end, which imports types only: not ids of the module; one home for those two names in the app is later work.
The file suffixes of the export formats (`<render id>-vertical.mp4`, `-square.mp4`), not the variant suffix of a render id.
The new-theme grammar without its cap, on purpose: the names inside stale work folders of earlier theme creations, which must be cleaned whatever their length.

Prune reads the run folders through the reader (L7.7) and keeps its lenient read for one case: a run.json the reader does not take as a record (a finished run without its end, a failed one without its error, a linked file) is still read as any object with a text id and status, so that a take prune could delete before the lot can still be deleted — leaving such a take alone is a change nobody decided. Where this read is stricter than before it only keeps: a file of a newer format is left alone, one that is no regular file or is over the reader's cap is not read. Its second read (L7.6b) is of renders/: a record file that is a link is not opened by the one reader of renders/, and is read through the link for the id, the take, the scenario and the creation time it says — never taken as a record — so that a linked record keeps the render and the take it kept before the lot.
entries: packages/engine/src/prune.ts → 2 own reads of a run folder's or renders/'s file

groups.reason: A reserved run is closed from outside on a lenient read of its run.json (its status alone decides): a record the reader refuses must still be closed, or it would say running for ever.
